split: The last three pādas of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, from 8.2.1 onward, are special. Sūtra 8.2.1 says: from here on, each rule counts as not having happened, as far as the earlier rules are concerned. Tap to see the split.
rajabhih: Here is why that matters. Take राजन् plus भिस्, by kings. A late rule, 8.2.7, deletes the न्, leaving राज, which ends in अ. Should the earlier rules for अ stems now apply? Try it both ways.
order: Inside the last three pādas, rules also run strictly in order, each blind to the ones after it. Watch रामस् become रामः. First स् becomes रु, then the final र becomes visarga. Try the opposite order.
passes: Programmers will recognize this. It is like a compiler with passes: the main grammar runs first, then the last three pādas run one after another. An earlier pass never sees what a later pass did.
